# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 46 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 46 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_046_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 3 — The Angel of Righteousness and the Angel of Punishment

**46:1** I said to him: "Lord, now that I have come to the end of these commandments, I ask whether it is possible for a man to keep them, given how great and demanding they are." "You shall keep them," he said, "if your heart is pure toward God. And all who have purified their hearts from the empty desires of this age shall keep them and shall live to God."

**46:2** "Lord," I said, "now that I have heard these commandments: if any man is unable to keep them because of the weakness of the flesh, what will happen to him?" "If he undertakes to keep them but does not keep them, and his heart is turned away from the Lord, he shall die. But he who undertakes them with his whole heart and labors to do what is right, even if he stumbles at times on account of the weakness of the flesh — this man shall live, because the Lord is compassionate."

**46:3** "The Lord sees that his heart is pure and has compassion on that man and forgives him all his transgressions. He strengthens the man and grants him to keep the commandments of the Angel of Righteousness, and so grants him salvation."

**46:4** "But for the man who lives in forgetfulness and does not keep the commandments of the Lord, the Lord hands him over to the angel of punishment, and that angel afflicts him for his wickedness and he is chastised with a view to salvation."

**46:5** "But Lord," I said, "how can the Lord be simultaneously so merciful and also permit such chastisement?" "Listen," he said. "The Lord is compassionate in all his works and in all his words. He is full of philanthropy and gentleness and forbearance and mercy. Therefore so long as a man repents, he has hope of salvation. But when he turns completely away from God and sins without repentance, there is no hope of life for him."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and soteriological precision.*
